SECTION F – INSPECTION PROCEDURE REFERENCE

This section is a reference for the inspection procedure used to produce the ratings recorded in Sections A–E of this form. It is intended to be used by all Holloway & Finch technicians performing inspections of ARRI Alexa Mini camera packages. The procedure is effective as of 2022-01-01 and supersedes all prior inspection guidance for this camera type.

F1. Purpose and Scope

This procedure covers the visual and functional inspection of the ARRI Alexa Mini body and its standard accessory package. It applies to all units owned or managed by Holloway & Finch Productions, including units on long-term rental. The procedure is designed to identify defects that could affect image quality, audio capture, mounting safety, or operational reliability. Cosmetic issues that do not affect function are noted but do not require corrective action unless they worsen.

F2. Equipment Required for Inspection

The following tools and materials are required to perform a complete inspection:

- Sensor cleaning kit (H&F-approved swabs and solution)
- Lens tissue and optical cleaning fluid
- Blower brush
- Magnifying loupe (10x minimum)
- Torque wrench with ARRI-standard mounting plate adapter
- Cable tester for SDI and XLR cables
- Lint-free cloths
- Flashlight or work lamp
- Inspection checklist (this form, printed or digital)
- Camera body cap and lens mount cap
- Battery dummy plug for firmware checks

F3. Inspection Steps

The inspection shall be performed in the order listed below. Each step must be completed and the result recorded before proceeding to the next step. If any step reveals a condition that requires immediate attention, the inspection may be halted and the issue escalated per Section F5.

Step 1 – Visual Inspection of Camera Body

Examine the camera body for cracks, dents, or deformation of the housing. Pay particular attention to the top plate, side panels, and the area around the lens mount. Check all screws and fasteners for tightness. Look for signs of liquid ingress, including residue or corrosion around seams and ports. Record any anomalies in the Condition Notes field.

Step 2 – Lens Mount Check

Remove the body cap and inspect the lens mount surface for scratches, burrs, or worn locking pins. Verify that the mount engages cleanly with a test lens or a lens mount test plate. Check the electrical contacts for dirt or corrosion. Clean with a dry lint-free cloth if needed. Do not use liquid cleaners on the contacts.

Step 3 – Sensor Inspection

With the lens mount open, inspect the sensor surface using a loupe and flashlight. Look for dust, scratches, or other contamination. If dust is present, use a blower brush to remove it. If dust persists or if any scratch or damage is visible, record the finding and escalate per Section F5. Do not attempt to clean the sensor with a swab unless you are certified to do so.

Step 4 – EVF and Viewfinder

Step 5 – Audio Inputs and Outputs

Inspect all XLR inputs and the microphone output connector. Check for bent pins, loose connectors, or play in the connector housing. Test each input and output using a known-good cable and a test signal. Record the condition of each connector and the result of the test.

Step 6 – Power and Battery Interface

Inspect the battery plate for wear or damage. Verify that the locking mechanism engages properly with a test battery. Check the power cable and any external power adapters for fraying or damage. Test the camera with the battery installed to confirm it powers on and off cleanly.

Step 7 – Media and Recording Functions

Insert a formatted media card and record a short test clip. Verify that the clip is recorded and can be played back. Check the media slot cover for proper closure and sealing. Record the test result.

Holloway & Finch Productions
Equipment Inspection Form – ARRI Alexa Mini (K1.0012345)

SECTION F – INSPECTION PROCEDURE REFERENCE

This section is a reference for the inspection procedure used to produce the ratings recorded in Sections A–E of this form. It is intended to be used by all Holloway & Finch technicians performing inspections of ARRI Alexa Mini camera packages. The procedure is effective as of 2022-01-01 and supersedes all prior inspection guidance for this camera type.

F1. Purpose and Scope

This procedure covers the visual and functional inspection of the ARRI Alexa Mini body and its standard accessory package. It applies to all units owned or managed by Holloway & Finch Productions, including units on long-term rental. The procedure is designed to identify defects that could affect image quality, audio capture, mounting safety, or operational reliability. Cosmetic issues that do not affect function are noted but do not require corrective action unless they worsen.

F2. Equipment Required for Inspection

The following tools and materials are required to perform a complete inspection:

- Sensor cleaning kit (H&F-approved swabs and solution)
- Lens tissue and optical cleaning fluid
- Blower brush
- Magnifying loupe (10x minimum)
- Torque wrench with ARRI-standard mounting plate adapter
- Cable tester for SDI and XLR cables
- Lint-free cloths
- Flashlight or work lamp
- Inspection checklist (this form, printed or digital)
- Camera body cap and lens mount cap
- Battery dummy plug for firmware checks

F3. Inspection Steps

The inspection shall be performed in the order listed below. Each step must be completed and the result recorded before proceeding to the next step. If any step reveals a condition that requires immediate attention, the inspection may be halted and the issue escalated per Section F5.

Step 1 – Visual Inspection of Camera Body

Examine the camera body for cracks, dents, or deformation of the housing. Pay particular attention to the top plate, side panels, and the area around the lens mount. Check all screws and fasteners for tightness. Look for signs of liquid ingress, including residue or corrosion around seams and ports. Record any anomalies in the Condition Notes field.

Step 2 – Lens Mount Check

Remove the body cap and inspect the lens mount surface for scratches, burrs, or worn locking pins. Verify that the mount engages cleanly with a test lens or a lens mount test plate. Check the electrical contacts for dirt or corrosion. Clean with a dry lint-free cloth if needed. Do not use liquid cleaners on the contacts.

Step 3 – Sensor Inspection

With the lens mount open, inspect the sensor surface using a loupe and flashlight. Look for dust, scratches, or other contamination. If dust is present, use a blower brush to remove it. If dust persists or if any scratch or damage is visible, record the finding and escalate per Section F5. Do not attempt to clean the sensor with a swab unless you are certified to do so.

Step 4 – EVF and Viewfinder

Inspect the EVF body for cracks or loose mounting. Check the eyepiece for scratches, cracks, or wear. Test the EVF display for dead pixels, lines, or other anomalies by powering the camera and navigating the menu. Record the condition of the eyepiece and the display in the Condition Notes.

Step 5 – Audio Inputs and Outputs

Inspect all XLR inputs and the microphone output connector. Check for bent pins, loose connectors, or play in the connector housing. Test each input and output using a known-good cable and a test signal. Record the condition of each connector and the result of the test.

Step 6 – Power and Battery Interface

Inspect the battery plate for wear or damage. Verify that the locking mechanism engages properly with a test battery. Check the power cable and any external power adapters for fraying or damage. Test the camera with the battery installed to confirm it powers on and off cleanly.

Step 7 – Media and Recording Functions

Insert a formatted media card and record a short test clip. Verify that the clip is recorded and can be played back. Check the media slot cover for proper closure and sealing. Record the test result.
